why: A = isHomotopyDirectLimit_of_level ∧ isHomotopyDirectLimit_truncation (universes 0): Lemma 2.1 (a level function f ≥ 0, f ≥ i+1 off X_i, makes the increasing sequence a homotopy direct limit) and Lemma 2.2 (X_Σ is the homotopy direct limit of its truncations, for ANY sequence). B = (1) for increasing S and such a continuous f, the graph lies in X_Σ, x ↦ (x, f x) is an embedding into X × ℝ and its image is a strong deformation retract of X_Σ; (2) for increasing S, X_Σ is the homotopy direct limit of {X_Σ^n}. A ⇒ B: (2) is A's Lemma 2.1 applied to the space X_Σ, the truncations and f = τ + 1; (1) is proved outright (straight-line homotopy in τ + upward closure; Mathlib isEmbedding_graph) — A states only the conclusion 'homotopy direct limit', not the strong deformation retraction or the embedding, which are B's extra (elementary) content. B ⇒ A: both clauses from B(1): the strong deformation retraction H onto the graph makes σ(x) = (x, f x) a homotopy equivalence (p σ = id, σ(p H₁) = H₁ ≃ id; Morse.IsHomotopyEquiv.of_leftInv_rightInv), hence p; Lemma 2.2 is B(1) for the truncations of an arbitrary sequence (always increasing) with f = τ + 1, so A's extra generality (no monotonicity in Lemma 2.2) is covered by B. Equivalent up to the elementary graph/retraction facts of B(1).
